title: The Crimson Throne
subtitle: A Crumbling Empire, a Vacant Throne, a Hundred Knives in the Dark
synopsis:
For three hundred years the Sanguine Empire of Veldoran ruled the river-valleys and marble cities of the Reach from the Crimson Throne — a seat carved from a single block of blood-red carnelian, set in the heart of the capital city of Coronne. The Vermeil dynasty that sat upon it was never loved, but it was feared, and fear kept the peace. Trade flowed down the great River Sangue, the legions held the frontier marches, and the Order of the Sanguine Communion blessed each harvest and each coronation with the same crimson rite. The Empire was old, and gilded, and rotten at the root — and everyone pretended not to notice.

Then Emperor Caius Vermeil the Third died in his bed with no wine in his cup and no wound on his body, and the pretending ended. He left no clear heir and a dozen claimants. His only acknowledged child, the Princess Severine, is young, clever, and friendless. His Lord-Regent, the chancellor Aldous Crane, holds the keys to the treasury, the granaries, and the city gates — and a smile that never reaches his eyes. His most celebrated general, Duke Roderick Valmont, sits in his frontier fortress with twenty thousand loyal soldiers and a grievance three generations deep. And above them all looms the Sanguine Communion, the imperial church, whose High Confessor speaks of 'renewing the covenant' in tones that make even hardened courtiers uneasy. Within a tenday of the Emperor's death the assassinations begin, the bread price triples, and the City Watch stops answering calls from the poor districts altogether.

The party does not begin as lords or champions. They begin as nobodies in the Shamble — the festering warren of slums that sprawls in the shadow of the palace — caught up in a murder, a fire, and a missing ledger that turns out to matter to very dangerous people. From those gutter beginnings they are drawn upward into a war fought not with armies but with poison, blackmail, forged wills, and whispered words at candlelit feasts. Each rung of the ladder reveals a deeper truth: that the Emperor was murdered as the opening move of a long game; that the succession crisis is being deliberately stoked; and that the Crimson Throne's three centuries of power were never a gift but a debt — a blood-covenant sworn by the first Vermeil emperor to something ancient and hungry that waits beneath the carnelian, and that debt is at last coming due. By the campaign's end the party will not merely have survived the intrigue. They will have decided who sits the Crimson Throne — and whether the covenant that empowers it is renewed in blood, or broken forever.
hook: It starts with a fire. The Old Quarter of the Shamble goes up a little after midnight — not the usual lantern-spilled accident, but three buildings at once, the kind of fire someone lights on purpose. In the smoke and the screaming and the bucket-lines, a man dies in the alley behind the Drowned Cat tavern with a Carmine Veil dagger between his ribs and a leather ledger clutched against his chest. He is still warm when you find him, and his last act before the light leaves his eyes is to press that ledger into your hands and rasp four words you do not yet understand: 'The cup. Tell Severine.' Then bootheels on cobblestones — someone is coming back for the body, or for the book, or for whoever holds it. Above the rooftops, across the river, the great bronze bells of the Sanguine Cathedral begin to toll the death-knell for an Emperor a tenday cold, and in the firelight the marble palace on the hill seems, just for a moment, to be the color of fresh blood. You are a nobody from the gutter holding a dead man's secret. By dawn, every faction in Coronne will want it — and you.

setting.name: The Sanguine Empire of Veldoran
setting.description: Veldoran is an ageing human-led empire built along the broad, slow River Sangue, a temperate realm of terraced vineyards, walled river-towns, white marble cities, and crumbling frontier holds that have not seen real coin from the capital in a generation. At its heart sprawls Coronne, the Throne City — a metropolis of a quarter-million souls where gilded palaces and domed temples crowd the high ground above a vast tangle of slums, tanneries, and flood-prone tenements known as the Shamble. The Empire's wealth is real but its institutions are hollow: the legions are unpaid, the granaries are mysteriously empty, the courts are for sale, and the great noble houses have spent three hundred years perfecting the art of murdering one another with a smile and a signature rather than a sword. Power in Veldoran does not march in formation. It moves through dinner invitations, marriage contracts, forged debts, poisoned cups, and the quiet work of the Carmine Veil — the guild of spies and assassins that every faction publicly condemns and privately employs. Magic exists but is rare, watched, and regulated by the church; a person who can throw fire is a weapon, an asset, and a suspect all at once. Over everything hangs the shadow of the Crimson Throne itself and the blood-covenant that empowers it, a secret the church has guarded for three centuries and that is now, at the worst possible moment, beginning to unravel.
setting.atmosphere: A world of velvet and rot, of candlelight glinting on poisoned rings. Veldoran is beautiful in the way of an over-ripe fruit one breath before it splits — marble facades streaked with grime, perfumed ballrooms built atop sewers, a starving city watching its lords feast. The danger here is rarely a monster in the dark; it is the warm smile of the person pouring your wine, the sealed letter that names you a traitor, the friend who has been bought. Tension is social and constant: every conversation is a duel, every favor is a debt, and the wrong word at the wrong feast can cost more lives than a battle. But beneath the human intrigue runs a colder current — the church's blood-rites, the crypts that hum with three centuries of stored sacrifice, the thing beneath the carnelian throne that dreams of waking. The Crimson Throne is a campaign where the players climb from the gutter to the palace one dangerous favor at a time, where allies must be made and tested, where a clever tongue is worth more than a sharp blade — until, at the very end, both are needed to decide the fate of an empire.

regions.name: Coronne and the Shamble
regions.description: The Throne City and the slums beneath it — a single sprawling organism of marble above and misery below. The high city is a place of domed temples, guild halls, and the palace district of Lord's Hill; the low city is the Shamble, a flood-prone warren of tenements, tanneries, gambling dens, and the lantern-lit Thieves' Market where the Carmine Veil keeps its safehouses. Most of the campaign's early intrigue is woven here, in tavern back rooms and tax-office cellars, where a clever party with no name and no coin can still learn a city's secrets. The City Watch patrols the high city zealously and the Shamble not at all, which suits the people who do their business in the dark.

regions.name: The Gilded Reach
regions.description: The estates, vineyards, and pleasure-gardens of the great noble houses, ringing the capital like a jewelled collar. This is the domain of the masquerade and the marriage-feast, where Houses Crane, Valmont, Aurelle, and a dozen lesser families pursue the succession war with invitations instead of armies. Beautiful, manicured, and lethal: the topiary mazes hide listening-posts, the wine cellars hide oubliettes, and a single dance with the wrong partner can realign the fate of the Empire. To move through the Gilded Reach the party needs invitations, sponsors, the right clothes, and the right lies — and the standing they earned in the gutter below becomes the currency that buys their way up.

regions.name: The Hollow Cathedrals
regions.description: The seat of the Sanguine Communion: the towering Sanguine Cathedral on the far bank of the river, and the vast crypt-city of the Sanguinarium that honeycombs the bluffs beneath it. Above, white-robed confessors preach the renewal of the covenant; below, in catacombs that descend further than any map admits, the church's inner circle — the Crimson Conclave — tends three hundred years of carefully hoarded blood and the old, patient thing it feeds. This is where the campaign turns from political thriller to gothic horror: incense-choked sanctuaries, bone-tiled vaults, blood-wards that drink the unwary, and the dawning understanding of what the Vermeil dynasty truly bargained away.

regions.name: Vermeil Keep and the Crimson Throne
regions.description: The ancient fortified palace at the summit of Lord's Hill, heart of the Empire and prison of its secret. Behind walls older than the dynasty, past the gilded audience halls and the warren of servants' passages, lies the throne room itself, where the carnelian seat sits cold and empty atop a vault no living soul is permitted to open. This is the campaign's endgame — the place where the succession is finally decided, where the Conclave intends to consummate the covenant, and where the party's accumulated alliances, enemies, and choices all come due at once. Whoever the party crowns here, and whatever they do with the throne's terrible bargain, will reshape Veldoran for the next three hundred years.

explorationRules: The Crimson Throne is an urban intrigue sandbox rather than a wilderness trek — the 'map' is the city of Coronne and its surrounding estates, and travel is measured in city districts and social standing rather than miles. The party moves between districts (the Shamble, the Thieves' Market, the Gilded Reach, the Cathedral precinct, and Lord's Hill) freely, but access to the upper districts is gated by reputation, invitations, disguises, or bribery — a ragged party cannot simply stroll into a noble masquerade. Track a Notoriety score with the City Watch: bold or violent action in public raises it, and high Notoriety means patrols, checkpoints, and bounties that make the high city dangerous to enter. Track Faction Standing separately with each of the five powers — Princess Severine's loyalists, Lord-Regent Crane's administration, Duke Valmont's military faction, the Sanguine Communion, and the Carmine Veil spy guild — because nearly every choice that pleases one faction angers another, and standing determines who offers the party shelter, information, jobs, and aid versus who sends knives in the night. Time matters: the succession crisis advances on a clock whether or not the party acts, and key events (assassinations, edicts, the masquerade, the church's rites) happen on schedule, so dithering has consequences. Between scripted scenario beats the DM improvises the living city — informants to be cultivated, blackmail to be gathered or buried, debts to be called in, Watch patrols to be evaded, fences and forgers and poisoners to be bargained with — and rewards social cunning, careful information-gathering, and well-chosen allies at least as richly as combat. Rests are easy to find but never truly safe; a safehouse is only as loyal as the faction that owns it.
